A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of SeedVR with matching main sections, equations and empirical material. v3 includes supplementary Sections 6–7 and Figure 5; this material is absent from v4, with no extraction gap preventing comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original restoration benchmark results, VAE reconstruction comparisons and attention-window experiments in Tables 1–4, plus qualitative restoration outputs.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark, VAE reconstruction and attention-window results in Tables 1–4 and the main qualitative outputs.

M1.justification: The Swin-MMDiT architecture, causal video VAE, training strategies and conditioning-noise procedure remain unchanged. Removing supplementary architectural explanations does not establish a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain mixed image/video training and evaluation on SPMCS, UDM10, REDS30, YouHQ40, VideoLQ and AIGC38. The omitted demo overview does not identify distinct data or task coverage beyond the retained real-world restoration setting.

E2.justification: v3 Section 6 reports video-demo comparisons against MGLD-VSR and VEnhancer; that reported comparison is omitted in v4. Comparator membership in the retained Tables 1–2 and Figure 4 is unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated training configurations, 720p evaluation preserving original video length, evaluation metrics and 12.5k-iteration window-size experiments are unchanged. No revised protocol is reported for the retained experiments.

E4.justification: The VAE and attention-window studies in Section 4.2 and Tables 2–4, together with Figure 4's illustrated cases, are unchanged. The omitted demo overview contains no distinct ablation, robustness test or specific error analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed details, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All values in Tables 1–4 and the main qualitative figures are unchanged. v4 omits Section 6's qualitative report that SeedVR outperforms MGLD-VSR and VEnhancer on real-world video demos. The underlying demo videos are not embedded in either supplied PDF.

T1.justification: The feature/window definitions and condition-noising equation in Section 3 are unchanged. The omitted supplement provides architectural exposition, without additional mathematical derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about arbitrary video lengths and resolutions, restoration quality, architectural contributions and inference speed exceeding existing diffusion-based methods by over twofold.

C2.justification: v4 loses Section 7's explanation of why whole-video text attention imposes resolution constraints and how text repetition and pooling preserve flexibility. Main interpretations of perceptual quality, REDS30 performance and window-size convergence remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The omitted supplement removes details of per-window text repetition and average pooling, Figure 5's normalization/modulation structure, and identification of the VEnhancer v2 demo checkpoint. Main training hardware, budgets, processing details and the project URL remain available.

R1.justification: v4 adds Zhou et al.'s 2022 blind face restoration paper as reference [81]. The introductory degradation discussion also cites Real-ESRGAN in place of RealViFormer. Previously listed works remain cited elsewhere, and the research positioning is otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 removes supplementary Sections 6 and 7 without relocating their text and adds an author contact email. Sections 1–5 remain essentially verbatim apart from citation edits, so the narrative revision is limited.

P2.justification: The detailed Swin-MMDiT diagram in Figure 5 is removed. References now begin below the acknowledgements, and printed page numbers disappear. Main Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–4 retain their displays and layout.

improvement.justification: v4 preserves the main scientific evidence but loses useful architectural documentation in Section 7/Figure 5, especially text repetition and pooling, and the demo checkpoint information in Section 6. This causes a limited decline in technical clarity and reproducibility that the small citation, contact and layout updates do not offset.
